shortDescription: By Emily Ou YongJapanese rubber futures eased on Thursday, paring gains after a sharp rally in the previous session, as peak-season supply increased and weak tyre demand weighed on prices.($1 = 159.8800 yen)($1 = 6.6703 Chinese yuan)

children: Japanese rubber futures eased on Thursday, paring gains after a sharp rally in the previous session, as peak-season supply increased and weak tyre demand weighed on prices.
The Osaka Exchange (OSE) rubber contract for April delivery
was down 3.1 yen, or 0.7%, at 437.7 yen ($2.74) per kg as of 0200 GMT
The rubber contract on the Shanghai Futures Exchange (SHFE) for January delivery
rose 310 yuan, or 1.62%, to 19,505 yuan ($2,924.16) per metric ton
The most-active January butadiene rubber contract on the SHFE (SHBRv1) gained 355 yuan, or 2.34%, to 15,540 yuan per ton

Top producer Thailand is emerging from the rainy season and entering its peak harvesting period, boosting supply and weighing on raw rubber prices, while tyre production remains weak from a year earlier, analysts at broker Shenyin Wanguo Futures said in a note

China's domestic passenger vehicle sales are projected to fall below 19 million units this year, for the first time since 2014, a Chinese auto association said on Wednesday, highlighting weakening demand in the world's largest auto market
Automobile sales could affect the pace of vehicle manufacturing, which drives demand for rubber tyres
Wednesday's sharp rise in Shanghai rubber futures was likely triggered by a World Meteorological Organisation report on El Niño, analysts from broker Minmetals Futures said in a note
However, there is no evidence yet of large-scale production cuts, and the weather premium could dissipate quickly if peak-season output materialises as normal, the analysts said
The front-month rubber contract on Singapore Exchange's SICOM platform for February delivery (STFG7) last traded at 248.3 US cents per kg, up 0.3%
